h: Planning a proper day on the estate
p: Mar Lodge rewards a bit of homework. The road west from Braemar runs out at Linn of Dee, and from there it's boots or bikes only, so think of the car park as your base camp. A popular lower-level walk heads up Glen Lui towards Derry Lodge, following a broad track through open glen with mountains rising on every side. It's a lovely half day for reasonably fit walkers and gives you a taste of the wild country without committing to the high tops.

Keep your eyes peeled for red deer on the hillsides, and red squirrels in the pinewoods. Golden eagles and other birds of prey are about too, though you'll need patience and a bit of luck. Binoculars earn their place in the rucksack here. Do give the Linn of Dee gorge a wide berth for swimming or scrambling, because the water is fast, cold and deep, and it's best admired from the bridge.

Practical bits matter in this corner of the Cairngorms. Mobile signal is patchy at best, so download maps before you set off and tell someone your plans if you're heading out far. In summer the midges can be fierce on still evenings, so pack repellent alongside the waterproofs.

Braemar itself is a brilliant place to finish the day. The village has cafés and pubs for refuelling, and Braemar Castle sits just outside it. Visit in early September and you'll find the village buzzing around the famous Braemar Gathering. Royal Deeside carries on east too, past Balmoral towards Ballater, so there's plenty to fill another day.
